decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display builds directly on the firm's core corrugated converting and display design knowledge, so it can read early market feedback and refine the product easily.
The pegboard-back shelf display is a close variant of the firm's existing cardboard display competence, and its results are easy to interpret within established customer channels.
The standard quarter-pallet display sits at the heart of the firm's knowledge base and serves as a staple format that it can improve using what it already knows.
The eighth-pallet display is a scaled version of a core format, so the firm can absorb market learning from it at low cost.

A wooden pallet lies outside the firm's paper and board expertise, which limits its ability to assimilate feedback and improve the product, but it still complements the display systems and was launched only recently.
The media-product display relies on familiar cardboard technology, although its niche market in shrinking physical media adds some risk.
